quote: he entered the consecrated place without due auspices; and the augurs, on the matter being laid before them, pronounced the appointment improper
notes: The consul Licinius's appointment of the day for assembling his troops was voided by the augurs for faulty auspices, so the Roman legions stayed in the city all year (livy:en:45:12).

quote: complaining that they were dispossessed of their lands by the Roman colonists
notes: Pisan deputies protested dispossession by the colonists of Luna, and the senate resolved the land dispute by sending five boundary commissioners (livy:en:45:13).

quote: that out of the four city tribes, they should openly, in the court of the temple of Liberty, select one by lot
notes: The censors Gracchus and Claudius disputed whether freedmen could be stripped of the suffrage and compromised by confining them all to one city tribe chosen by lot, the Esquiline (livy:en:45:15, dispute begun at livy:en:45:14).

quote: Cneius Tremellius, a tribune, protested against it, because he had not been chosen into the senate
notes: The tribune Tremellius, passed over in the lectio senatus, vetoed the censors' customary request to prolong their term for building contracts (livy:en:45:15).

quote: that Macedonia should be divided into four districts, each of which should have a council of its own
notes: The senate framed the constitutional settlement for conquered Macedon - nominal freedom, dissolution into four republics with councils, halved tribute, and closure of the gold and silver mines to shut out tax-farmers (livy:en:45:18).

quote: he requested a grant of Aenus and Maronea to himself
notes: Roman senators courting Attalus tried to induce him to seek partition of his brother Eumenes' kingdom, but after Stratius's counsel he asked the senate only for Aenus and Maronea (livy:en:45:20, intrigue at livy:en:45:19).

quote: without first consulting the senate, and without acquainting the consuls, of his own sole judgment he proposed to the people the question
notes: The praetor Juventius Thalna tried to rush a declaration of war on Rhodes past the senate straight to the people, and the tribune Antonius blocked it, dragging Thalna from the rostrum (livy:en:45:21).

quote: that they should neither be declared enemies, nor any longer remain in alliance with Rome
notes: After the Rhodian envoys' suppliant appeal and Cato's speech in their favour, the senate ruled Rhodes neither enemy nor ally and stripped it of Lycia and Caria (livy:en:45:25, appeal from livy:en:45:20-24).

quote: the Macedonians should live free; possessing the same cities and lands as before; governed by their own laws
notes: At the Amphipolis convention Paullus and the ten commissioners proclaimed the new constitution - four districts with separate councils, halved tribute, bans on intermarriage and on working the gold and silver mines (livy:en:45:29, elaborated livy:en:45:30 and 45:32).

quote: Aulus Baebius alone was condemned for having lent Roman soldiers as agents in the butchery
notes: In the inquiry before Paullus and the commissioners into the massacre of 550 Aetolian leaders, the Roman commander Baebius alone was condemned for lending soldiers for the killing (livy:en:45:31, massacre reported livy:en:45:28).

quote: instigated them to attend in full numbers, to give their votes, and to take revenge on a haughty and morose commander
notes: Galba, a tribune of the second legion and personal enemy of Paullus, mobilized soldiers resentful over small booty donatives to vote down their own commander's triumph (livy:en:45:35).

quote: When the tribes which were first called in gave a negative to the question, the principal men in the state ran together to the Capitol
notes: The first tribes voted to reject Paullus's triumph after Galba's speech, until the leading men pressured the tribunes to restart the proceedings so Servilius could speak (livy:en:45:36).

quote: all the tribes, when recalled to give their votes, passed unanimously the bill concerning the triumph
notes: Servilius's speech, baring his scars, shamed the soldiers into reversal and the recalled tribes passed the triumph unanimously; Paullus triumphed three days with Perseus led before his chariot (livy:en:45:39, speech at livy:en:45:37-39, triumph and deaths of his sons at livy:en:45:40).

quote: requested the senate to allow the hostages to be ransomed, at any price that should be judged proper
notes: Ambassadors of Cotys of Thrace appealed to the senate to ransom his son and the hostages, and the senate returned them gratis to display Roman dignity (livy:en:45:42).

quote: He further desired that the alliance with him might be renewed
notes: King Prusias came to Rome in person, congratulated the senate, renewed his alliance, sought the disputed Antiochene territory, and commended his son Nicomedes (livy:en:45:44).
